en.html:
Higekiri plunged into the rear approach. A small but definite interval behind him, I followed.

I had blocked his retreat—at the beginning. Even when I stopped his acrobatic tactics and began pressing him, the sole entrance should have been behind me.

Then—when!

...While we were measuring our distance!?

Pretending to prepare one final counterattack, he had actually been securing his escape!!

en.html:
He was right. I had become so absorbed in the fighting that I had forgotten the larger situation.

Only I needed to finish my opponent quickly. He had merely to escape this underground space alive, and his conditions for victory were fulfilled!

How had I forgotten that?

No... Perhaps the astonishing thing was that the Grand Commander had remembered. Attacked by an unknown man, his life in danger, and still so composed.

Was this the distance between a green youth and an old campaigner?

en.html:
Death filled the place.

Soldiers.
Armored warriors.
Attendants.
Priests.

The shogunate's people aboveground. Hachimangu's people. Without discrimination, with an equality beyond improvement, all had received the same fate: death.

No life existed.
A quiet, smooth, peaceful world had appeared.

An ice field.
The wilderness of the far north.

Beginning and end coexisted.
An immovable, unchanging closed world.

Not one glance for the Grand Commander.
Her face turned straight toward me.

Hikaru.

...Two years.
Since I had seen her in the flesh, this close.

Considering that interval, and her age, she looked surprisingly little different from the figure in my memory. Enough to make me feel somehow out of step.

Why was there so little change?
Why was she so much as she had been?

When Hikaru's star had changed with such ferocity!
